title: From user language to an allowlisted Rails query
outcome: Turn a proposed intent into previewed filters without executing generated SQL.
cue: Interpret language. Resolve identity. Apply only known filters.
version: Provider-neutral principles · Ruby 3.3 / Rails 7.2 lab · legacy Ruby 2.7 adaptation notes
useCase: Turn a proposed intent into previewed filters without executing generated SQL.
benefits: A clear decision and a way to check it.
drawbacks: A schema-valid foreign ID or unknown field can expand access if passed directly to where. Blind name matching can also give the user the wrong valid record set.

trace.title: User wording
trace.detail:
## Understand

Natural language can be ambiguous. A model can propose status and depot_name; application code decides whether those fields are supported and resolves names within the actor's scope.

Never let the model choose tenant identity, arbitrary column names, joins or SQL.

Use explicit result states: accepted filter, needs clarification, unsupported request, or unavailable model. Show the applied fields in human-readable chips.

If there are two permitted depots called East, ask which one. Do not resolve ambiguity by searching all tenants.

The filter object should define its own validation and query conversion. That keeps model output away from ActiveRecord internals and makes the same filter usable through a manual form.

Test language interpretation separately from deterministic filtering.

trace.title: Follow one input
trace.detail: Bound request → propose intent → reject unknown fields → resolve permitted names → preview normalized filter → run authorized relation → exact count. Test zero/one/multiple name matches and an unsupported request.

trace.detail: A schema-valid foreign ID or unknown field can expand access if passed directly to where. Blind name matching can also give the user the wrong valid record set.
